title: Rate hikes, not cuts: oil and inflation reset the autumn mood
dek: The ECB raised rates, Fed minutes pointed to another hike, Brent pushed past $106 on Middle East supply fears, and Korean shares fell more than 8% in a week.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.explanation: The VIX — the options market's gauge of expected swings in the S&P 500 — sat at 15.51 on Monday, down about 9% over the month, and high-yield credit spreads were a contained 3.15 percentage points on 8 October, yet CNN's Fear & Greed index was still in "fear" at 45. Reddit chatter was split between broad index funds and a cluster of chip and data-centre names, a sign that enthusiasm is concentrated rather than general.

regions.headline: Hiring slows, but the Fed is still talking about hikes
regions.summary: September payrolls came in at 29,000 with unemployment at 4.2%, while minutes of the Fed's September meeting pointed to at least one more rate rise this year without urgency to move in October. Inflation at 3.71% in August and a 10-year Treasury yield above 5% keep borrowing costs high: the 30-year mortgage averaged 7.40% on 8 October.

regions.headline: ECB lifts rates to 2.5% as energy costs bite
regions.summary: The ECB raised its deposit rate to 2.5%, with euro area inflation at 3.23% in August and a Reuters poll pointing to another move in December. German industrial output rebounded at its fastest pace since early 2025, though Italian output fell. The euro slipped to $1.12, which cushions exporters but adds to the cost of dollar-priced oil.

regions.headline: Korean shares slide, India hikes, Japan's new PM talks down reflation
regions.summary: The KOSPI fell 8.4% over the week as foreign investors sold tech heavyweights amid doubts over the AI build-out. India's September inflation jumped to 5.54%, a near two-year high, after the RBI's first repo rate rise in nearly four years. Japan's Nikkei is up 8.7% in a month, but the yen remains weak at 158.63 per dollar.

watchNextWeek: US September CPI, with the Fed's Beige Book later in the week
IMF–World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok, plus speeches from Lagarde and the Fed chair
China September trade and inflation data
Monetary Authority of Singapore policy review and Japanese data
IEA and OPEC monthly oil market reports
body:
## Opening

This was a week in which the direction of travel on interest rates became unmistakable, and it is upwards. The European Central Bank raised its deposit rate to 2.5%, minutes from the Federal Reserve showed officials expect another increase before year-end, and India's central bank had already lifted its policy rate for the first time in nearly four years. Behind all of it sits energy: Brent crude rose 6.45% over the week to $106.79 on Monday as the Iran war and attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply in question. Equities took it calmly — the S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,811.54, up 1.15% on the week — but the calm is uneven. Korea's KOSPI fell 8.42%, small-cap US shares slipped, and CNN's Fear & Greed index, which tracks seven measures of investor positioning, remained in "fear" at 45.

## United States

The labour market is cooling without cracking. September brought just 29,000 new jobs, [below expectations](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxOb2U4XzdJcWZXWXZHTHAyYnI0Q3BGSEloNTJVb3NKOTVCM1VEemo2UmtUX0pOSzkyek1hcVU4QktIWkpYTmlzZ0RmR3hjczdISGJkQm1BeU5ZbVpGSUdrdXp0SWpkMDlHSExfc29KV1lJcy01SmZaVkJGV3cyLTZCM0NhN0pGSEU5bFlxOU43T2I2bDlCM3NmSXdrTVpYSXdB?oc=5), and the unemployment rate ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%. Yet weekly jobless claims — new applications for unemployment benefit — are [hovering near a 57-year low](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxPMWFoUC1DSlZwckJETlF2WXdjTnhwSkt5UlIxVzBMQVoxVXJ0UjNTdjBDdmlwUmR3V2hQWDBGaTNnLTd1X2VIQVhBcVFmZGJHNGtCODU3RE55eHk2Y0FBbVBEUXF1S2lDaW42Y2VnUk9aRExvMXM1TGFIYjNpcnhTSUc5S1V3Nk1KWkZrSDlyTUFpNTZqYWxraw?oc=5), so firms are hiring less rather than firing more.

That mix leaves the Fed arguing with itself. Minutes of the September meeting, at which rates were raised to a 3.75% average for the month, showed policymakers [expect a further increase but see no urgency to act in October](https://news.google.?oc=5). Governor Waller said [more hikes are needed, with "flexibility" on the pace](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipgFBVV95cUxNVlJjTS1oeE1aRmVEcC05dTZkd25ONVRidzJkTlozaEE3Q0tvQ2hPd0dYemMxNWUzTUZORnFfb0FWZUdDOVp3QUVwelQ5cjJzcV9oMl9mZmpCTnJOaGh6XzZXLXlxOWJBUVhTX05oOVhwS2hhZG1WbmppWlRRRGNDOGZneGNneTRiLXBhVHd1Z3FGc1JaZC14Qm14SVRlYi1Cd3MxSjVR?oc=5), while another senior official [cast doubt on a move this month](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxNckNMd0xCc1RMemJpSlNXQVBEeVFKUktQWmFwTlBZWTFrM19DWTA1d1dtN3djS0tSbTY3VzhWYlp2NEdpQ1RIdUthT2xGMVhPNmxqRXFyUEloVVNRQWZ6S3VQeHlZaklEbGh2SWRmckNONnZXaV81TjItOTAwZlBPakZsTzRoVHpMUDVEYlFpbTJraXM?oc=5).

Why it matters for households and businesses: inflation was 3.71% in August, up from 3.54% in July, while core inflation (stripping out food and energy) was 2.76%. The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.24% on Monday, down 1.34% on the week in level terms, and the 30-year mortgage averaged 7.40% on 8 October. Borrowing is not getting cheaper. Reuters framed the mood neatly: [a wealth boom and a price shock colliding](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxOdUhraTJpN1hiM1QxNXN1OWFiMEFJVjRPQnhZdXV0TW0ya0FvdEdVLWRPQUFVVXFiX2hvTUJYcFBwYlBxR1N2OXhCTW13UjdteTNmTTJkbVNGTVFzaTlwbFM1bkdTTGtuN2dqbEE3WUVmQldzZzZSdlRkOUFJTldWRzRyRTJuNVhCRXpBZExnN0lFY0E?oc=5).

## Euro area

The ECB [raised rates to 2.5%, citing energy costs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNV0tWM0xZcmxXSUZReDVWQ0NycWY2ZW5ZaVFEdjh0SmtWWHRCMjVLdTVvV1dKRTNZX1FTeEZxNUxtQjR1LWJmeE5kLUFiT2NWZ1hBU0tEWXVXNHMwX3NUZnZHbUU5aUNMcExtejVEejhEOURxb2ZVa2daVnFZZ0dWclZXZ0ZOb3RJX2trQk9PcFIwSzdIcHpEY01GNzVwSjdQdGZTbTNDR3FEQQ?oc=5). Euro area inflation was 3.23% in August, up from 2.93%, and a Reuters poll of economists [expects another hike in December as inflation runs close to double the 2% target](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirAFBVV95cUxPNVlkaVBmN0lBelRFMEktcDh1aG5GZElENVRtWngwa1VzQ0pRaFU5bU9mQnE0ZDVna3JFRVV3ZW1qZHgxYlNvRUJLWmV4WnVxbWhwWVRKLVdfVzBNbFhLSlU4NmhSMmxSQi1hYTF4U1ZJQ3dGNjRNUklHMHY5ZjJEamZ4ZXVkT3J0X3VaVGNQSkJzNWtVNVZuTlVURFZWYnRJdmdtS3hpQ0kzVl9W?oc=5) — though some policymakers and the published account of September's meeting [dampened bets on a near-term move](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxNY0lSVTF5NmlCRnNxLXFhU29BeFZYdnVCUGU4cU1PWnVRV1VjUU40NEZDZFhYNEVULWJCbVFTaTJ1UEJPRlhKZk8tc2NQVE1Pa0ZXblpUSzkyYUx6M0VTS1BQUDFhNlBOSnNWN3dZYy1SejZ3Snl4dnZPeTVoS1lWa1pjMk9DZUlzSlkyb0x6Qms1VkdSWEIyZ2hIU2FrQ04zQzJELTB6MEM3dw?oc=5).

The real economy is mixed. German industrial output [rebounded at its strongest pace since early 2025](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxObHhBSUs0enRTWUQyZ3JxdzlmdUFkN1hHSTNINmJQQzl2cUJVWEE5RkMtUm9wRDNPLWJTRUlnTzgybkw3UTdqVXRhdkFqaklDdDc4WThmbDdWRTNEVUlxa25JSzYtQlk3S2RaaGtobnc3bUQxNXFjZGNNU3BncUVwRG4walJsc3dWTlFrLVlOeEpVbjlWZ0ZrS1JhMktibzN6RTBuazFOc1hESXlFd0RJ?oc=5); Italian output [fell unexpectedly in August](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijAFBVV95cUxQTlVHREM0SVBiX2NXX0paZU5Kbi1PYzFYU3o0U3IybzYzakRleEZ0T0Zoc282WDczaVBXa05McGIzbVo4eWM1Y2g1UjlqalZzUXdkVVdMbkppM1FCLTQyVVVnaHV2R0NMMFNZd2JQWlFvY3c0NkFUSElWUWJhaVFNZWphRk5NQ3hPeUlNYQ?oc=5). Unemployment held at 6.4% in August. Trade is the live political question: the EU and China [reached a preliminary deal to curb hybrid car imports](https://news.google.?oc=5), and Brussels is weighing [how to counter Beijing without alienating partners](https://news.google.?oc=5). Separately the EU [adopted nearly 1,600 new sanctions listings targeting Russia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxQNHU4aWdseGJQNDlHSkY2bVlVakhtNG9qSWo2eHl0MV9WSTRoc1lqdUdTcHlXeWdCVU1nZ3V6c2Z2dV9FMmRXdGlmMjhOOVpENE9ZRkY1UkRxM1ZzUTBaLTE0OUhEUE9nVzFVd1pUQUlJcjljeWhjNEJvSk55VlhobmU5Q0F2S2lKb0M0Z2lLcjg1Y1J2bG8zUU8xUXdLUV93WUpOMG5DSE11dzJmdklv?oc=5).

For businesses, a euro at $1.12 — down 3.56% in a month — flatters export earnings but makes dollar-priced oil and gas dearer at exactly the wrong moment.

## Asia

Korea was the week's outlier. The KOSPI dropped 8.42%, with [foreign investors dumping tech heavyweights as doubts about the AI build-out spread](https://news.google.?oc=5) and [a 5.4% single-day fall](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxPdkgtM1FmVWpvUDFiVEVMMUhCdzFzX3RUTElzR3VWLUk1VE1rcHN4YXROY0lhWXVrd1JQVTNuUzdPWU5QMkRtdzFWWXFmVjh0eTJfN05TaVJkX3BBdzI5eERic3FDaWlkVXIyMS1nVmhxWFhYaWRLdUpUMGRCck9HMXFCaHNITkkyVElyZllzRXNFc25VeGtrczROYUc2LVFZS3BNc2NMUTUtNFh4czBIUTYzNWdJeURCOXc?oc=5) over the weekend's sessions.

Japan went the other way: the Nikkei is up 8.72% over the month. Prime Minister Takaichi has been working to [shed her reflationist label](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipwFBVV95cUxQY19WdmpQRTdkTjZNLUtOOGtxZkd4Tzg5V0QxS1lsVXFGcmRuYUg3RWlraXI5QUtLX2JDZHMySEJrajRmVVNBVDZWR0lWalIxYUEwOV81UEw0TDQ3eGlDVG9CazV3V0NueER6VkczTWtETkxZanRBUWVoZkZDa0syOU5LMUQzdTBjcV8zZUNHVk1IZzVVamVFekFUUVRIMWRjVDJEMnlrNA?oc=5), saying [the economy does not need reflationary policy now](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijwFBVV95cUxPSjVReTNVQlN6ZGY5ckVPSXp5VHlRNGZVdkRKbjU0b1dRX3BFYXNSVXJPR3FOZGE4VzNIaUw3WGpjaTNiMGhIeHdSdlRPSlVsb2lsa0xhbFJlY3F6VG1DNGFmb0syaXF5U0pDcmhnQjlUQmV6bHQtNFBRWFhibkNDOVFwYW1EVFc0UWl0RVVGOA?oc=5) and vowing to [watch the yen and prices carefully](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxOQS1EUGVuWGlkTDBsY3pYcXZKOER0c25xbUFQbklLemN1S1ZGaVY3bVNYTDQtYURmX01JZXdUVzdEdmZOcnhvWEloUFBjR0ZqSER6S3QwUE9oZVJoZGpjS3NKMmRYanI0ZHdNNE5wb1BTUFg1czd2Zjl0YlZaZ3RId1hFQWxpNkVCc0g1TkVRUnA1ZUlDQklZRGoyeUVkdGtDWjBELTEyelV2QjZtREczQkVR?oc=5). The yen is still weak at 158.63 per dollar, and a Bank of Japan dovish dissenter [signalled support for future rate rises](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxPR2UwTVJzRWJmT0w3NFVxUm9kUV9wOThHRUNBQm9tRUlnZWNIeXVHNlB1MjQ5ZWROekRaQjd6aFZQamVrOTYwWnpvOUlETjNiMWNkZVc3VmRSUW83bjhJMnhnWEIxeVBzRXE4bEdPMGc1amZENWRRY2NwX29pRHpGNFdHTDFSY1hvaE9tSUlXRVhZOHB1YlhFU3FTU0Z3UFZubDJscno0TWpRamRKVGR1RHZ3?oc=5).

India's September inflation jumped to [5.54% from 4.83%, a near two-year high](https://news.google.?oc=5), [strengthening the case for more hikes](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxOM2hyc2tfZ1c4OFc2WGEwN3J5Ri1jaWVLOWtWbmpYTzlMcnNyVVhrN0pEdGg1ZXlKdEJMRjNiNXpRRC1KVDNXaWdDQ0ptQ245VEJaY19RZVNMUGJDYTJjUGNwV2NrLTU0LTRVbEcwWGZmSzhoX3hEdkVGcHAzTGZLb285UTBwYXhxZTVSWmxRNkt3X2xISDZwZg?oc=5) after the Reserve Bank's October increase. In China, electric and hybrid vehicles reached [a record 61.6% of new car sales in September](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiWEFVX3lxTE1VUkY3NTBGVXRyektmVlJwcklNSEJrNlk2VGRXQlowMzdJR0hHZG9Hd1FYOFlFODgtQ0hkZTdfLUszUG9XNVBfNlhxbDctZmYxSWxqS1VwS2w?oc=5), while exporters [turned on the taps](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxNTnF0ZjNPSjZ1S2RQQjAxTUQxSC1GRmNmdVR0d0wyc3gzMFZCNVhQbGJhOHVZSWZFeHJJUno3MWVxNnZocGl1YnltRlJ3ay0wTl9MazhJaFpaZlVTMnNJQnRtWkdHTFVzSU9RNkQ4YWRZUnVkSXJYTVpXQzVma2kwR1QwRDNlR1VDSzBnaFl5MFdfazhsbGRSYXppbndnc2h6WjFVZGN0M3lOWjQxYVZEb3ZDdExJR3M?oc=5) in metals markets.

## Debt and politics

The US federal budget deficit for fiscal 2026 [hit $2 trillion, the largest since Covid](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifEFVX3lxTE85bjl2RjFrTU1Ed3I3LXJoT3pBRXoyalQ4MDd2Z1FvMVZWcXVTQjkzTm5PaF9tZEs4SVRRRnhGd0RwaG9NVWZpUlY2YmNXUEJxbnF1Vk1UMjh6N1p4UzdMdk8yRUFEbHMybE83XzZwMDF6V1dEdUlBS1BldjE?oc=5), with the shortfall at 5.77% of GDP in 2025 and federal debt at 122.59% of GDP in the first quarter of 2026. The trade deficit [reached a 17-month high despite tariffs](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifkFVX3lxTE41cmdCYWpkdGxsdVd6M0pGSTJDU3R2RXhvaS1sTFU4d0xpSi1LVlVNUWRRYUhFR2tkZUpBUVQ0cjF4ZkszZ1hYUXV5RW5EUXUwbHdkbUVTV0xYSk9fbkRJLUh5YTNCQjd1blh1OXNZY3djRG5pREYtb3dPeGpRdw?oc=5), and the President [blamed a Supreme Court tariff ruling for lost revenue](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxPWTdPTERsZlZmU3lSVGh3dHhlMVhFUkUyZjJvaXl4ZUhTLWlpSkpkSlppUWZtVGVncU9neE1HLVBRNDdKaEswc2xXS292eG5LVlltZXl6R09rZHdsbllWZUt1RUdSLXgxZ3U3ZTZTdTJIelMzQlNoRFRHeHE3eHhlOWRfc0tNWGthbGNOYTg5UTdGNUw0WnJyQl9rdlE1TlV0SGc3RXAzVE9JV19aTzR0S3IzN3lzdDdscFE?oc=5). Ahead of the midterms, Washington also [struck a deal with Moscow for Russian diesel](https://news.google.?oc=5) — a sharp policy reversal aimed squarely at fuel prices — even as Ukraine's president said Russia [continues to strike energy facilities](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqAFBVV95cUxOYk9yd3EweHFPQ2doVnFxQmxCdEJxMmdBdF9FT2tzdExGZmR3eUo0TjFyTmU0azY4UEtmRW56djNGaERmMGdpcmNHZWRPcllwdEhPUVhsNjJqMzYxRko2dXA0VTBtdGZvYUdid1hZZkFMeGtJOGdVX1J0NUU5X29naUJaUVNxMG9LWEw2Q3prUHVTNTlyanVIbjFxOE80Y3oyNTlfX3VhT2U?oc=5).

Debt is the theme of this week's IMF–World Bank meetings in Bangkok, where [the Middle East war and high debt levels will dominate](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivgFBVV95cUxQWlZqTVZkYlUxR2xKODRtSHFhLUI5ZVk4MWlwUURPZTRJSy1UYjdKak1ZbzdGMG80dmNOTVlVbUtvbW1zUU9hWE5QeU9xc19wWE50TnR4M05sQ0c0aFI0ZmYtTGN6Q0hwanJUajNzSlRfaVBQNXdPMUlfQlpfb1JHTGlQWkg5aVdOTE5SZ29NRXZLSW85enZHa2dCOVFSWmFpUEptcWMxa1JxVW15ZGhLLTRRcDEyeXBEWkw0RnJR?oc=5) and the institutions are expected to [warn central bankers of a gathering storm](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxPM2tWc2xGT0Voa21HekR4eTZIM3Y0ckRVUFVTTnhDVnhXajk3SnJCODd4enpuUDE0YU80MkVvRmxGNm95YVdlSi1PVzI2MVlJSDZXRTA5UUZ1UnI3aG9YQ0lPN1RrRWZWR2VnemhtM3RnSzViZ0ZTT3FyTzVRZW9GMktjZWs?oc=5). Euro area government debt was 88.9% of GDP in the first quarter, up from 87.7%.

## AI and technology

The IMF said AI investment is [keeping global growth around 3% while bringing massive disruption](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwgFBVV95cUxONXItVGZaTjNISE9iMlVzZzhlV2ZmYzFDR29feFhfWFRhRzJFdWlwYXk5QkZpUHQ3WVhLZEZId2xobTNmc1E2Y25FN2c1TTg1eldiR3RLR003ajh2RUpSN1RxYXVzYjJ4TW5ZMW1ZcVljRndfSUpoNVVlLUE3eWc1MkhqUUtGQTdYdC1zVUxIbnNJWVJYb2ZIcVN1S3QzWWhQUmdsQ3VFVG9xSEs4NDVvOTZ5dHJRZUNNaUtsazVSMThYQQ?oc=5) — a reminder that one spending cycle is now doing a lot of macro work. Microsoft's president warned that [AI is less regulated than milk](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxNakhDNFlaMk9mSGQwbi0zcWlFSW1hQVRUckFFekhNbWF0MUVHSFVFNUhDYXRicUpQV1dTcEFka2RsNXk2a2tYV21NcUJOWWFJU09NTjNMVlBjOHBHa0tfRW1UTUJpRFl3bE96LUZTZzhFUm8waHR0dTdHZmlmd2E4dTQ4bWRKY3dlWUR2RkpUOW42clIwUUxYa0ZsTHNZT0JyRW9NNWY3c0c0Rk5QSTFJcm9McnFfMThhdnoydEE5WQ?oc=5), and Bill Gates called [cyberattacks the most imminent AI threat](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimAFBVV95cUxQQlk1MEkxSmlfblJNdU1oY1l1NlFCMWQ1VTN5RHRkQkgyclF4aV9WcGJHODdZTTJSTldVcDdtd0xfX0pHcDJyZkZxaEU4aW1hY2FFb2JpNDJFd2dRcUJVek9OUVVJWF81U1hEY09iNlQyd0l3RHdfV0JfMzFRMkNjQnhPSjFvTUJDeWVrZUFMX3JWNldJbFpqMg?oc=5). Analysts are increasingly focused on when the money runs into limits: one survey of Wall Street views argued AI is [heading toward a cash-flow negative inflection point with spending slowing in 2027](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxPZHJZa2RsX3JhdE1DYWtLd3hzYmRmSnFfc3J1VE1MeTJQYUdaS2VIbXpGUTk0NGx3bFl6SmZ1TllHMDA1RnBGcHEyeTQwNmFmUEtSTm9BRHVObWtQN3N5VmJEZGxVSGtaUnU0SVIwb2hpTkNqenlRVFp6WVYxYjZEb00zYUtqb28t?oc=5). That debate, not chip demand itself, is what Korean equity investors appeared to be reacting to.

## Company news and results

Constellation Brands reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 results in its SEC filing: net sales of $2,633m, up 6% on a year earlier, reported operating income of $805m, down 8%, and reported earnings per share of $3.32 against comparable EPS of $3.74. The company updated its fiscal 2027 reported EPS outlook to $11.85–$12.55 and reaffirmed its comparable range of $11.20–$11.90, and disclosed the acquisition of the ready-to-drink brand SpikedAde for $75m at close plus up to $278m of contingent consideration ([filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/16918/000001691826000039/stzex991_83120268kearnings.htm)).

Elsewhere, Volkswagen said vehicle deliveries [fell on continued weakness in China](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiqgFBVV95cUxPZzJBXzlIMDhad3lKUGpmSHAtZ1h4cjZVbjZ6cEZxTE0tYUhaNWszRWZtYlNlOXN6UTIxZkJFazJ5SUZCV25ZSjhEY1c1STJuRXdtTV80Ri15NFR1Z1ZVYWdjOS1hbzVpSE5oRE4wNEd6dTMxdlpfVFFoRzV0NG9Neml0VEJlZnNMTWhZbTNJbXRubEdXOTFyWmg1eEhwMFAtWG4yN3YzSk5RUQ?oc=5) — a datapoint that matters for German industrial output and for the EU's trade stance. In deals, quantum-computing firm IonQ agreed to [buy a cybersecurity company for up to $1.3bn](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxQNmk5NnMzd2lyOHZSR1dvNEVleUIzdGg0dTF0X3NkWDVNblZYMXVoQjJFREtXdE10MFYwZkpOZHptN3dYdFV2S1RwMzAyNFFqMkxqX3N3c3lpSVNUU0s4U2hlaTVNNFg1RTJ5RkZpb1JyUGFKTFc3bHFlWkV3S0szdDUtSlE2WV91VmphdUdZc3MyNTM1YTVpVlNnNW04QUIyMmQxTGx2Z2FBcGFFZ3Q0anEzeFJlNHpXNUdheDBXRQ?oc=5). PepsiCo, Delta Air Lines and Levi Strauss all filed quarterly results with the SEC during the week.

## Market mood

Volatility stayed subdued: the VIX, the options market's gauge of expected S&P 500 swings, was 15.51 on Monday, roughly 9% lower than a month ago. Credit markets agree — the spread on US high-yield bonds, the extra yield riskier borrowers pay, was 3.15 percentage points on 8 October, barely changed on the day before. The yield curve (the gap between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields) was a positive 0.44 points, normal rather than recessionary.

Yet the Fear & Greed index sat at 45, in "fear", versus 44 a week ago and 33 a month ago. Reddit chatter — unverified opinion, useful only as a mood gauge — was dominated by broad index trackers alongside a burst of mentions of memory chips, semiconductor funds and data-centre power names, with speculative satellite and crypto-adjacent tickers also in the mix.
